pains.title:
Agents are smart
But their memory is short
pains.lead: Three situations everyone who works with AI agents knows
pain1.title: Every agent starts from a blank page
pain1.text:
Claude Code figured out how the project builds
Codex has no idea, neither does Cursor
You explain the same thing for the third time
pain1.fix:
All agents write to one memory and read from it
What one agent concludes is available to the rest at once
pain1.figure: Diagram: knowledge of five different agents flows into one shared memory and back out to all of them
pain2.title: Knowledge stuck with one person
pain2.text:
Anna's agent found why the build fails
The agents of Max, Lena and Ivan never learn about it
Tomorrow each of them loses another hour on the same error
pain2.fix:
A record in the team memory reaches the agents of every member at once
And you see who made it and through which agent
pain2.figure: Diagram: a record made by one member's agent spreads to the agents of the whole team
pain2.record: The build fails on Node 20 — Node 22 is required
pain2.status.author: author
pain3.title: The session stayed on another computer
pain3.text:
All day you worked through a task with an agent on your laptop
In the evening you are at another computer, and the conversation stayed behind
You have to retell the whole context from scratch
pain3.fix:
Close the laptop, open another computer and carry on the same conversation
The session history is already there — every step and every conclusion
Sessions are turned on per team when wanted: they weigh more than memory
pain3.figure: Animation: the laptop closes and the same conversation with the agent continues on the desktop
pain3.chat.agent1: Migration 042 holds a lock on the orders table
pain3.chat.agent2: Picking up where we left off: splitting migration 042 into three lock-free steps
how.title:
Three steps
And your agents remember
how.s1.title: Create a team
how.s1.text:
Open the cabinet and create a team
As many people in the team as you like
how.s2.title: Connect an agent
how.s2.text:
In the cabinet, get a one-time code for connecting your agent
On your machine, run one command — it will ask you for that code
how.s2.note:
The token never appears on screen
It goes into a file only you can read
how.s3.title: Agents remember
how.s3.text:
The agent searches the memory and saves to it itself
A record from one agent is seen by the whole team
teams.title:
Everyone sees their own
and nobody does it twice
teams.lead:
An analyst, a tester and a developer work in one memory
Each has their own sections and their own inbox, and the list of work is shared
teams.access.title: Access to one project
teams.access.text:
Open one project to a person — they see no other, not by name and not by search
The guest's agent recognises the project folder by its repository address and connects its memory
You grant the rights: read, write, search past sessions
teams.roles.title: Roles and sections
teams.roles.text:
Project memory is split into sections: the tester sees theirs, the analyst sees theirs
For a role, a section that is not theirs does not exist: search does not find it
Roles and section rights are set in the cabinet
teams.roadmap.title: Shared roadmap
teams.roadmap.text:
An agent takes an item — a second one cannot take it
An item with a dependency waits and opens by itself once the dependency is closed
Let an item go — leave a note: what is done and where you stopped
teams.desk.title: Desk: records instead of comments
teams.desk.text:
A finding for another role goes in a record, not in a tracker comment
A spec mismatch goes to the analyst, a recommendation to the tester
Each role has its own inbox, and one person handles a record
The author gets a reply, and emails go out on the record's steps
teams.process.title: Business processes
teams.process.text:
One scenario is implemented in several projects on different stacks
An agent sees how it is done in the others before doing its own
The "rules × projects" matrix shows where a rule is implemented and where it differs
teams.local.title: Your machine's page
teams.local.text:
The command opens a page on your computer: the projects it syncs and the actions on them
The memory map shows sections, records and the links between them
The page is reachable only from your machine
teams.note: A team owner turns the paid modules on in the cabinet
trust.title: Memory you can rely on
trust.history.title: Nothing gets lost
trust.history.text:
Every edit of a record is kept in git
Two edits of one record never overwrite each other
trust.infra.title: Your own server
trust.infra.text:
Memory lives on the project’s server, not a big cloud
An encrypted backup is made every night
trust.mcp.title: Any agent over MCP
trust.mcp.text:
Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and others speak MCP
Your memory is not tied to one agent
trust.token.title: Token off screen
trust.token.text:
An agent gets its token for a one-time code
The token sits in your own file, revoked in the cabinet
agents.title: Works with the agents you already use

pricing.lead:
The price is per team per month
As many people in the team as you like

Before that, an archive of the memory comes by email

weight.title:
Memory and sessions
Weigh differently
weight.lead:
A team gets memory at once and turns sessions on with a switch when it wants
Both share the room of the plan
weight.memory.name: Memory
weight.memory.what: Short findings of agents: rules, decisions, pitfalls
weight.sessions.name: Sessions
weight.sessions.what: Whole conversations with an agent, with the output of its tools
weight.sessions.state: A switch on the team, off by default
weight.example: A real example: a project with 88 sessions
weight.note:
Try sessions — the room they take shows on the team page
Not for you — turn them off, and the server deletes the team's sessions while memory stays
For you — take a bigger plan
weight.figure: Comparison: the memory bar is barely visible next to the sessions bar
faq.title: Short and honest
faq.agents.a:
Any agent that speaks MCP
Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Zed, Cline, VibeIDE, VibeIDEA and any other MCP client
Each agent connects with one command and gets its own token
faq.storage.a:
On the VibeMemory project's own server, not in a big platform's cloud
The server makes an encrypted backup every night
Agent tokens stay on your machines in files only you can read
faq.builtin.q: Why is this better than an agent's built-in memory?
faq.builtin.a:
Built-in memory lives inside one agent
Here one memory serves every agent and the whole team
And with history search allowed, an agent also finds the past conversation where a conclusion came from
faq.sessions.q: How do I continue a session on another computer?
faq.sessions.a:
Turn sessions on with the switch on the team page, and the vibememory program carries them between your machines
Open the same agent on another computer and go on with the conversation
Sessions are heavy: one project gathers hundreds of megabytes, so they are optional and take the plan's room
faq.parallel.q: What if I worked on two machines at the same time?
faq.parallel.a:
That is the normal mode, not an exception
Histories merge record by record, and both branches of the conversation are kept
Nothing gets lost silently
faq.team.q: How many people can a team have?
faq.team.a:
As many as you like
The price depends on memory size, not on the number of members
A team has three roles: owner, admins and members
faq.payment.a:
This is a pilot project, so payment is a bank transfer with a comment
As the project grows, we will move to payments through a legal entity
You can start with the free 50 MB plan
changelog.title: Changelog
changelog.meta.title: VibeMemory changelog
changelog.meta.description: What is new in VibeMemory: releases, features and fixes
changelog.0.13.1.title: Moving a machine into its own personal store
changelog.0.13.1.summary: A machine leaves a borrowed personal store for its own: the split runs in steps with visible progress, and git no longer hangs on long errors
changelog.0.13.1.details:
The owner of a personal store pushes their machines' settings and catalogs into it
personal split runs in steps and prints its progress instead of staying silent for minutes
git no longer hangs on long error output
changelog.0.13.2.title: Safe project moves and protected routes
changelog.0.13.2.summary:
project move shows a plan and waits for explicit confirmation
personal split can be resumed: the new store's quota is checked before the move
changelog.0.13.2.details:
project move prints a migration plan and waits for an explicit --apply: nothing moves silently
Diagnostics separate machine errors from store rejections and reveal nothing extra
Sending data to someone else's personal store is blocked, not just flagged in a report
personal split can be resumed: the new store's quota is checked before the first change
Projections of rights and routes survive the move
Routes of protected projects stay protected during a move
changelog.0.13.3.title: Personal skills stay on your machine
changelog.0.13.3.summary:
Personal skills are saved locally, not to the store
Sharing and unsharing ask for explicit confirmation and never touch the local copy
changelog.0.13.3.details:
skill save with the personal level writes the skill to a local folder, not the store
skill share and skill unshare show a plan and wait for explicit confirmation
Sharing and unsharing go in a separate commit and push, the local skill stays as it was
Removing a skill from the store does not delete its local copy
A pending unshare is visible in status and doctor: it never comes back silently
changelog.0.15.0.title: The server asks an outdated engine to update
changelog.0.15.0.summary:
A machine tells the server its engine version
The server refuses pushes from a too-old engine and asks to update
changelog.0.15.0.details:
The refusal comes before any data is received: an old machine does not send megabytes over the network for nothing
An admin can stop pushes of a single machine
The machine owner sees a notice in the cabinet and gets an email "update the engine: vibememory update"
Skill findings log: an agent appends to a skill what it did and what it learned, skill_get returns the latest findings
rules audit gathers the rules of every level and asks an agent to find contradictions
The server owner gets a morning email with product and server statistics
changelog.0.17.1.title: Sync gets through on a flaky connection
changelog.0.17.1.summary:
When the connection drops mid-push, the machine sends its data in small portions
What already arrived is not sent again
changelog.0.17.1.details:
A portion that fails is halved until it gets through
Failed attempts back off with a growing pause instead of repeating every two minutes
A machine whose store on the server is still empty sends everything it has collected
doctor says the connection drops in the middle of a push
changelog.0.17.0.title: Memory comes to the agent with the question
changelog.0.17.0.summary: Fitting project memory records are attached to the agent's question, and memory search ranks by relevance
changelog.0.17.0.details:
With each question the agent gets up to three best-fitting project memory records
A record is not repeated within a session; threshold and count are set in the config (promptMemory)
Memory search (memory_search) puts the best matches first and shows their score
After context compaction the agent gets the project's open hand-offs in full
changelog.0.16.1.title: Skill checks call skills the way an agent does
changelog.0.16.1.summary: vibememory skill eval runs on Sonnet by default and counts a called skill
changelog.0.16.1.details:
Phrases run on the sonnet model by default: it picks skills the way a working agent does
A skill call counts even when claude exits with a non-zero code after it
Another model is set with --model: a short name leads to its current version
changelog.0.16.0.title: Checks you can trust and skills that fire
changelog.0.16.0.summary: vibememory check proves a project's checks were run, vibememory skill eval shows which phrases trigger which skill
changelog.0.16.0.details:
vibememory check run runs the checks of .vibe/checks.json and keeps a receipt with a fingerprint of the code
vibememory check verify says whether the receipt is fresh: if the code changed after the run, it is stale
vibememory skill eval sends phrases to the model and shows which skill it called for each
vibememory doctor names closed hand-offs whose decisions were not carried to memory, knowledge or rules
changelog.0.15.1.title: A machine tells the server its current engine version
changelog.0.15.1.summary: Before every trip to the server the engine checks the clone's ssh setting against its own version
changelog.0.15.1.details:
A machine connected by an older version names its version right after vibememory update
The version does not get stuck after later updates
The cabinet's window for connecting an agent or a machine starts with installing: lines for macOS, Linux and Windows and a link to Download
changelog.0.14.3.title: A push over the quota no longer fills the server
changelog.0.14.3.summary:
The server cuts a push as soon as it outgrows the store's quota
The machine pauses such pushes and says how much does not fit
changelog.0.14.3.details:
One push brings no more than the store's quota and no more than 1 GiB
A cut-off receive does not pile up on disk: the nightly repack clears its traces
A machine whose push the server cut for size retries once an hour, not every two minutes
doctor says the push is over the quota and where to raise the plan
The server's owner gets a mail when a machine keeps sending a push that cannot be accepted
And when the server's free disk shrinks faster than the threshold within a day
changelog.0.14.2.title: Skill and rule headers fix themselves
changelog.0.14.2.summary:
A skill whose header trips an agent is not saved silently
vibememory headers fix shows what to change and changes it with --apply
changelog.0.14.2.details:
Before writing, the engine checks name, title and description of skills and rules
A colon with a space, a hash or a special first character breaks the header for a strict parser
Such a file is not written, and the engine says what to fix
A description after a hash used to be cut silently, the fix brings it back whole
vibememory headers fix without --apply shows the plan, with --apply it fixes personal skills and rules
An agent can save a skill with fix: true — the header is written fixed
doctor names the skills and rules worth fixing
changelog.0.14.1.title: Desk and processes in the personal store
changelog.0.14.1.summary:
Hand-offs to yourself and processes work without a team
Modules are turned on in the cabinet, the server picks them up without a restart
changelog.0.14.1.details:
Desk and process modules are turned on in a personal store the same way as in a team store
The memory server takes the enabled modules from the access snapshot at once, without a restart
Records are still written only by the server, the client does not edit them
changelog.0.14.0.title: Skills update themselves from the set
changelog.0.14.0.summary:
skill check shows which skills are out of date and what changed
Untouched skill files update themselves, your edits are never touched
changelog.0.14.0.details:
skill check compares personal skills with the VibeBrains set: was → now for every skill
skill update shows a plan, and with --apply updates the untouched files
skills.autoUpdate turns on updates on tick, once a day
A file you edited stays yours and only shows up in the report
Skills and rules got roles: a team member sees what is addressed to their role
A newcomer to the team sees only what was picked for the start
A project is renamed with a plan, routes are added and removed with a plan too
The panel got a tab for skills and rules
skill remove without --apply only shows what would be removed
changelog.0.13.5.title: Clearer memory and project controls
changelog.0.13.5.summary:
Doctor sees only running memory servers
Projects are removed with a plan, while records and the memory map explain themselves
changelog.0.13.5.details:
doctor distinguishes several live MCP servers of one agent and does not ask to restart closed clients
project remove shows a plan and removes a project from memory without losing local files
Project buttons and statuses explain their actions and states
The memory map explains record types and the link graph
Records get a title in the person's language instead of the technical id
changelog.0.13.4.title: The changelog reads right in the terminal
changelog.0.13.4.summary:
The --changelog flag shows what is new before the engine is even set up
--changelog <id> opens the full record and links to the public changelog pages
changelog.0.13.4.details:
vibememory --changelog prints the latest changes with the ids of the releases
vibememory --changelog <id> shows the full record of one release
No engine setup is required: a newcomer sees what is new from the first run
Records link to the public changelog pages on the site
